data.body: Operator 2026-09-29: 'Make ddflow to promote and recommend to the agent to execute the tests in the workflow as relevant and as parallel as possible'. Original B16: 'Choosing which tests to run by reasoning about the change is guessing — derive it.' And targeted sweeps hide standing breakage (a full run found 12 pre-existing failures invisible to every targeted gate), so the full suite stays at the gate. Scope: (a) services/testselect.py: the tests relevant to a diff (base...HEAD plus the working tree): changed test files, tests importing a changed module or anything that transitively imports it (Python AST import graph over the repo), and tests named after a changed file's stem; each with its reason; (b) a parallel command to run them, derived from the configured unit_tests command (runner prefix + its options + the files), -n auto when xdist is declared; (c) 'ddflow tests [--item] [--base]' CLI + ddflow_tests MCP tool, following the pins shape; (d) the driver says: while implementing run 'ddflow tests' (relevant, parallel) after each change; the unit_tests gate runs the WHOLE suite, in parallel; (e) gate status for unit_tests names both; (f) leftovers from B-parallel-tests: doctor passes the repo root to the workflow check so the serial-pytest advisory shows there, and the init template / ddflow_configure text propose 'pytest -q -n auto'. The selection is fast feedback, never a pass: it is advisory, and the gate still runs everything.

data.summary: reviewer_independence recomputes a reviewer's family from the MODEL NAME via [agent].families and ignores the family declared on the [[reviewer]] (review.Reviewer.resolved_family's 'declared wins over guessed' rule): a Qwen served under the alias google/gemma-4-31B-it (root Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, self-reports Qwen/Alibaba, declared family alibaba) is counted as 'google' at complete time. Harmless when both differ from the author, wrong when the alias names the author's family.

data.body: Measured 2026-09-29 on the LAN critic (vLLM, ~35 generated tokens/s per request while serving two): 2371 chars 624 s, 5436 chars 1133 s, 8190 empty completion, 30000 timeout; reasoning_effort low / enable_thinking false come back off contract. So a 44k-char diff is ~9 sequential chunks x ~1000 s = ~2.5 h. vLLM batches concurrent requests, so aggregate throughput rises with concurrency while per-request speed drops far less. (a) [[reviewer]].max_concurrency (default 1 = today) runs up to N chunks at once, results assembled in chunk order; (b) total_budget_s applies to the wall clock, not the sum; (c) partial/unavailable accounting unchanged per chunk. Measure before/after on a real diff.
data.title: Review a diff's chunks concurrently: a slow local reasoning model takes ~0.2 s per diff char per request, and chunks run one after another

data.consequences: Until [worktree].local_files lands (needs ddflow/config.py, held by B23), roborev in a worktree falls back to the global default_agent (kilo, kilo's own default model). kilo share was set to disabled so reviews are not published to opncd.ai.
data.context: Operator 2026-09-29 chose 'local file, copied' after the global-config route was shown to leak. roborev has no machine-local per-repo file of its own and reads .roborev.toml from each checkout.
data.decision: The committed repository carries .roborev.toml.example with the project's review guidelines only. The working .roborev.toml (agent, model -- e.g. a LAN deployment's served name -- reasoning levels, guidelines) is git-ignored and lives in the primary checkout; ddflow copies it into every worktree it creates via [worktree].local_files. roborev's GLOBAL config holds only default_agent/default_backup_agent: a global default_model or reasoning level leaks into other repos (probe 2026-09-29: a global default_model was handed to claude-code in a repo pinning agent='claude-code', model='', and broke its review; reverted). Supersedes committing the LAN pin (B-roborev-lan-qwen, commit 08dc353/4be8018): per D-no-own-services-committed.
data.title: roborev's agent, model and reasoning are machine-local: an untracked .roborev.toml, copied into worktrees; git carries a generic .roborev.toml.example

data.body: Decision D-roborev-local (operator 2026-09-29). roborev reads .roborev.toml from each checkout and has no machine-local per-repo file, so an untracked copy must reach each worktree. (a) knob [worktree].local_files = [] (repo-relative paths); (b) worktree create copies each existing one from the primary, never overwriting a file already in the worktree, and never a TRACKED path (refuse at config load: a tracked file is not local); (c) status/doctor note a listed file missing from the primary; (d) this repo sets local_files = ['.roborev.toml'] in its git-ignored local config. Test: a new worktree gets the copy; a tracked path is refused.
data.title: [worktree].local_files: git-ignored machine-local files (e.g. .roborev.toml, .claude/settings.local.json) copied from the primary checkout into every worktree ddflow creates

data.summary: Every worktree whose branch predates a NEW config knob can no longer commit or run ddflow: the git hook sets PYTHONPATH to the primary but 'python -m ddflow' puts the CWD (the worktree) first on sys.path, so the worktree's OLDER ddflow code loads the primary's NEWER .ddflow/config.toml and Config.load raises 'unknown knob enforce.forbidden_trailers' (after B-forbid-trailers merged, 2026-09-29). Commits are refused for a reason unrelated to them; the workaround is merging main first. Same family as B8ea7a90aea / L-gate-cmd-vs-branch-deps (config from the primary, code from the branch). Fix: run the primary's code in the hook (python -I / an absolute module path), or let an unknown knob degrade to a warning when the config is newer than the code.
